# Independent audit: sharp all-dimensional simplex roof

Audited source:
`candidate 5e5b642b770e6623`.
Dependency read in full:
`candidate 588e75e8ff86db2e`.

**Result: PASS, all sections, including strictness and sharpness.** No
repair was identified. The source verifier passes 288 exact checks. The
independent `supporting computation verify_sharp_all_dimensional_roof_audit_slab_recovery.py`
passes 8,057 exact reconstructed-vertex, determinant, strictness, and
optimization checks. These supplement, rather than replace, the following
arbitrary-dimensional proof audit.

## 1. Coordinates, measure, and arbitrary partial columns

The map x=y+t e, with y in ker(v_0) and v_0.e=1, has Euclidean Jacobian
1/||v_0|| relative to dH_(d-1)(y) dt. Thus the specified transverse measure
is exact even when e is oblique. Every simplex section lies in [-d,1].
The condition h>d gives h+L>0 on every section, including those near the
lowest vertex.

On a nonempty B column, h+U_B=ell_B+h+L_B and L_B>=L. Since
0<=ell_B<=ell, it follows that h+U_B>=r_e ell_B. This treats partial
columns correctly; it is not restricted to complete T columns. Extending
ell_B by zero outside its projection gives integral ell_B=b. The pointwise
dual inequality follows separately for r_e>=lambda and r_e<lambda, with
ell_B<=ell in the latter case. Boundary columns have zero transverse
measure and do not alter the integrals.

## 2. Exact affine overlap and the small-lambda range

F_lambda preserves each transverse line and sends its interval [L,U] to
[(1-1/lambda)L-h/lambda,(1-1/lambda)U-h/lambda]. Both endpoints move
downward because L+h>0. Its intersection with [L,U] therefore has exactly
[ell-(h+U)/lambda]_+ length. This proves the dual identity with the
correct factor lambda, without an omitted determinant.

In barycentric coordinates q_i=(1-v_i.x)/(d+1), the sum of positive
longitudinal derivatives is sigma>=1 because r_0=1. Along an actual chord,
q_i(L)=q_i(U)+r_i ell/(d+1). Summing the positive coordinates and retaining
q_0(U) gives sigma ell<=d+U. Since (h+U)/(d+U) decreases in U when h>d,
its minimum at U=1 is (h+1)/(d+1)=beta. Thus r_e>=sigma beta. This handles
all lambda<=sigma beta by giving zero overlap volume. At the threshold
a lower-dimensional overlap need not be empty, but no emptiness claim is
made or needed.

## 3. The affine overlap polytope is exactly the computed simplex

For lambda>sigma beta, the inverse map adds (t+h)/(lambda-1) times e.
Facets with r_i<=0 remain satisfied automatically, since t+h>0. The
additional positive-facet inequalities are precisely

    q_i+a p_i q_0>=a p_i beta,
    a=1/(lambda-1), p_i=(r_i)_+.

The transformed coordinates mu_i=q_i+a p_i q_0-a p_i beta satisfy

    q_0=(mu_0+a beta)/(1+a),
    (1-sigma/lambda)mu_0+sum_(i!=0)mu_i
                                      =1-sigma beta/lambda.

Both coefficients used as divisors are positive in the stated range.
Every nonnegative solution reconstructs original q_i>=0: its mu_0 is at
most (lambda-sigma beta)/(lambda-sigma)<1<beta, hence q_0<beta and
q_i=mu_i+a p_i(beta-q_0)>=0. The reconstructed coordinates sum to one.
For p_i=0 the original and transformed coordinates agree, and the
negative-derivative inverse facets were already automatic. Thus no
original simplex inequality has been dropped.

The independent mu_i, i!=0, form a full simplex of scale
D=1-sigma beta/lambda. The independent q-to-mu Jacobian is

    det(I-a p_nonzero 1^T)=(lambda-sigma)/(lambda-1)>0.

The rank-one determinant computation is valid in every dimension. The
fixed physical-to-barycentric Jacobian cancels against V. Hence the
actual overlap volume is exactly

    V*(lambda-1)/(lambda-sigma)*(1-sigma beta/lambda)^d.

This also agrees with direct reconstructed-vertex determinants in the
independent verifier; the source's separate vertex enumeration checks
all original and inverse-image inequalities in dimensions two to four.

## 4. Direction comparison and strictness

For sigma=1, the exact overlap is V(1-beta/lambda)^d. For sigma>1 and
lambda>sigma beta, define x=(sigma-1)/(lambda-1) and
c=beta(lambda-1)/(lambda-beta). Then 0<x<1, c>1, and 0<cx<1. The ratio
to the sigma=1 expression is (1-cx)^d/(1-x)<1, since
(1-cx)^d<=1-cx<1-x. In the remaining range beta<lambda<=sigma beta the
actual overlap volume is zero whereas the reference is positive. Thus
strict comparison holds at every finite lambda>beta when sigma>1.

The condition sigma>1 is exactly the presence of some other positive
v_i.e, because r_0=1. The statement's strict-direction criterion is
therefore correct and exhaustive for this comparison.

## 5. Optimization, endpoint, and no extremizer assumption

The function d eta^(d-1)-(d-1)eta^d increases continuously from zero to
one, with the stated positive derivative in the interior. Hence eta is
well-defined for every 0<b<=V. For b<V, the finite choice
lambda=beta/(1-eta) yields exactly

    lambda[b-V(1-beta/lambda)^d]=V d beta eta^(d-1).

This is a legal chosen dual parameter, not an unproved optimization or
compactness assertion. Finite-lambda strictness gives the strict roof
bound whenever sigma>1 and b<V.

At b=V, expanding the finite degree-d expression gives the limit Vd beta.
For sigma>1, the exact overlap formula instead gives the strictly larger
limit V[d sigma beta-(sigma-1)]. Its difference from Vd beta is
V(sigma-1)(d beta-1)>0. Since every finite-parameter dual expression is
a lower bound for the same fixed roof, its limit remains a lower bound.
No body or cap limit is taken. The endpoint strictness is justified.

## 6. Actual convex sharp examples and chord dependency

When sigma=1, only facet zero has a positive directional derivative;
thus U(y)=1 on every positive chord. The independently read chord source
proves the exact tail distribution by the actual overlap T intersect
(T-s e), which is a translated homothety of T. Its layer-cake derivative
has no positive-level atoms, including the maximum length m=d+1 for
d>=2. The resulting upper-level columns have exactly the mass and
transverse measure used by the roof proof.

The chord length ell is a nonnegative concave upper-semicontinuous
function on the convex projection. Its positive superlevel set is compact
and convex. Cutting T by the inverse image of that set therefore gives
an actual compact convex subbody. For eta>0 it has positive volume and
hence nonempty interior; this remains true when the maximum-length chord
lies on a boundary face of the projection, as can happen when some
r_i=0. The formula does not require the maximum chord to be interior.
For eta=1, B=T gives equality directly. Thus sharpness holds for every
prescribed b, not merely along an approximating nonconvex family.

In dimension two, V=9/2 in canonical coordinates and
b/V=2 eta-eta^2; the bound becomes H[3-sqrt(9-2b)], agreeing exactly
with the earlier planar roof theorem. The result is an ordinary
continuous geometric input. No integer-base replacement, all-direction
center selection, or OC constant is inferred from it.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
